articles.title: The 15 best cat toys to prevent boredom and bad behavior, according to experts
articles.summary: The best cat toys are from Amazon, Chewy, Petlibro and Catit. Learn how often you should play with your cat, if catnip toys are safe and why laser pointers are bad for cats.
articles.body: Chasing after a plush mouse or digging treats out of a puzzle aren’t just fun activities for cats — they’re actually beneficial for their health, says Dr. Abel Gonzalez, the clinical director at Dutch, a pet telehealth platform. Cat toys prompt felines to mimic their natural predatory behaviors like pouncing and chasing, which is mentally and physically stimulating for them. Using toys to play your cat also strengthens the bond you share, leading to a more trusting relationship. I talked to experts about how to shop for the best cat toys and rounded up their favorite options, as well as those NBC Selected pet parents recommend. Experts also shared tips about how often to play with your cat, and explained why a laser pointer is the worst toy you can buy. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best cat toys in 2026 Best overall cat toy All the experts I spoke to agree that a wand like this one is the best overall toy for cats. While shopping for one, prioritize models that have a prey attachment at the end, meaning something cats can hunt, like feathers, which mimic a bird, says Sandra Grossmann, the owner of The Feline Consultant LLC. Jennifer Van de Kieft, a certified advanced feline training and behavior professional who owns Cat Advocate, a feline behavior consulting company, recommends slowly pulling the toy away from your cat and encouraging them to go after it. There is a catnip ball covered in feathers at the end of this wand, which is attached via velcro. As your cat swats and grabs at the wand, they work to detach the ball from the ribbon — when they finally do so, they feel good about themselves and it builds confidence, says Van de Kieft. I own this wand toy and whenever my cats “catch” the ball, they pick it up in their mouth and run away with it, bringing it to their bed or swatting it around my apartment. Best teaser toy While wand toys with a prey attachment are best, you may also want a model like this one. It allows you to mix up playtime, ensuring that cats don’t get bored or come to expect the same toy. The Rainbow Cat Charmer is a NBC Selected Pet Award winner and Rebecca Rodriguez, former NBC Selected editorial projects manager, says her cats Luna and Enzo love playing with it. “I’ve bought my cats many wands, but this one is by far their favorite,” she says. “As soon as I pick it up, they run over to play. When I need a break, I squeeze the wand between the arm of the couch and they’ll play with it by themselves.” Best catnip toy “My cat Wonton loves this banana so much that he is on his third one,” says Lauren Swanson, NBC Selected editorial director. “If given the option, he would choose this toy over my husband and me.” The banana-shaped toy is 6.9 inches long, covered in a textured cotton twill fabric and filled with organic catnip. Wonton kicks it with his back legs, as well as tosses it in the air and catches it. My cats rub their faces all over this toy and tend to drool on it, which causes the yellow fabric to stain. But that doesn’t deter them from playing with it over and over again. You can purchase the Yeowww’s banana toy, a NBC Selected Pet Awards winner, individually or in multipacks. Best silvervine toy Silvervine is an alternative to catnip, but because it’s more potent, cats are more likely to respond to it, says Gonzalez. These chew toys are made from thick silvervine sticks, raffia palm and sisal rope, textured materials that clean teeth, according to the brand. They also have pieces of gall fruit on them, which grows on the silvervine plant and helps with digestion. You can purchase the toys in packs of three or six. Best kicker toy In the wild, cats grab, hold and kick their prey after they catch it — kicker toys like this one are designed to engage that behavior at home. I bought the 20-inch long plush snake for my cat Wanda about four years ago and I still frequently find her attacking it. It’s thick so she can comfortably wrap her front and back legs around it, and there’s a pocket I add dried catnip to. Best mouse toy “My cat is obsessed with toy mice, but she also destroys every toy she gets her paws on,” says Leah Ginsberg, former NBC Selected managing editor. “She loves these catnip-dosed little guys because she can chase and chew them. I love them because they’re cheap enough to constantly replace.” SmartyKat’s plush mice are designed to mimic real mice with their soft bodies, felt ears and dangling tails. Experts recommend hiding them around your home to engage your cat’s seeking instinct. They’ll follow the smell of the catnip, which encourages them to hunt each mouse out until they collect them all. You can purchase the mice in packs of three, 10 and 20. Best ball toy Cats love toys that make noise, according to our experts. They’d hear their prey in the wild, so a toy that offers auditory stimulation gets them excited to hunt. These mylar balls crunch and crackle, and they’re lightweight, so cats can easily pick them up with their mouths or paws. “My cat Enzo goes crazy at the sound when I crinkle them in my hand,” says Rodriguez. “He’ll swat them around my apartment, running back and forth, and it’s one of the only toys he’ll pick up in his mouth and carry around.” The multicolored balls come in packs of six, 12 and 24. Best toy with multiple attachments Cats can get bored of their toys if they don’t periodically change, says Grossmann: “If they’ve played with something ten times and it hasn’t lost a feather, it’s not interesting anymore.” To avoid disinterest, look for toys with swappable attachments, like this one from Leo’s Paw. It comes with a base you stick to a flat surface and a wire you insert inside. You clip one of the five included birds onto the wire, suspending it in the air for your cat to jump and swat at. The bird swings around as your cat plays with it, which mimics a bird flying above their head. Each of the included birds looks different, giving your cat something new to hunt whenever you swap it out. I’ve owned this toy for about four years and it’s one of my cats’ all-time favorites. I swap the birds out every few weeks, or when I notice them losing interest. The suction cup base adheres to my floor pretty well, but it unsticks from time to time. I find that the included sticky pads you can use with the base are key to helping it stay put, plus they don’t damage my floors. Leo’s Paw also sells replacement wires and bases. Best spring toys I’ve never met a cat who doesn’t enjoy chasing after these plastic springs, which Van de Kieft says are fantastic toys. “It’s like a ball, but something about it is even better,” she says. “It has more visual interest, and unlike other inanimate toys, all you have to do is walk by or brush it and it starts moving.” My cat Lucy sprints across my apartment with her springs, swatting them around or carrying them in her mouth. She also brings them to me to throw, initiating a game of fetch. I buy this pack of 12 multicolored springs and give Lucy two at a time so I have replacements when one inevitably disappears under the refrigerator. Best toy for kittens “Kittens will play with just about anything that moves, and something like a butterfly flutter toy is particularly exciting for them,” says Van de Kieft. This one is motion activated, so it catches cats by surprise when they pass it. The toy is built with a sensor that detects motion when cats are nearby, causing the toy’s butterfly to start moving and its base to rotate. The toy automatically turns off after it stops detecting motion to preserve its battery. The weighted base has non-slip pads to keep it sturdy as your cat swats at the butterfly. The toy comes with two butterflies, and you can purchase additional replacements separately. Best toy for adult cats Adult cats benefit most from toys that let them engage in strategic hunting, like snuffle mats, says Grossmann. The mats have textured fabric stitched to them, creating pockets and folds you can tuck dry cat food or treats into. Cats have to use their sense of smell to locate the treats and dig for each one, which creates a brain game that mentally exhausts them over time. You can also sprinkle dried catnip on top of the snuffle mat, or spray it with liquified catnip. Pet Parents’ circular snuffle mat lays flat or cinches semi-closed, which makes it even more challenging for cats to find food. The bottom of the mat has an anti-slide backing so it doesn’t move around on your floor, and it’s machine-washable. The snuffle mat is available in three colors: gray, green and brown, and gray and blue. Best puzzle toy Similar to snuffle mats, traditional puzzle toys like this one, a NBC Selected Pet Awards winner, also make cats work for their food. The puzzle has 16 cups you add treats or dry food to and cover with swiveling leaves. Cats then have to figure out how to move each leaf out of the way to retrieve their treat. You can also place treats inside the puzzle’s red pegs — when cats slide the pegs over a cup, the treats fall into them. Nikki Brown, NBC Selected senior editor, bought this puzzle toy for her adult cats, but says kittens can use it, too. “The puzzle encourages cats’ hunting instincts and it forces them to eat slower, which has always been a struggle for my cats,” she says. “If you have more than one cat, I recommend getting two puzzles so they’re not fighting over it.” Best electronic toy This electric toy is one of Van de Kieft’s favorites for adult cats, but those of any age can use it. The base has a feather wand attached to it with a piece of fabric that sits on top. When you turn the toy on via a button, the wand spins in unpredictable patterns, causing the fabric to rustle and move. My cats watch the toy, suddenly pounce on it and whack at it. They also love seeing the built-in lights flash, and I appreciate that I can customize how fast the wand moves. If your cat starts to lose interest in this toy after a while, Van de Kieft suggests putting packing or tissue paper over it. Doing so adds another barrier over the wand and makes an engaging crinkling sound when cats jump on it. Best tower toy Despite owning this toy for a while, Rodriguez’s cats still love it. “Every time I think they’ve gotten bored with it, they start playing with it all over again,” she says. “My cat Enzo and I will volley the balls back and forth for about 15 minutes.” The toy tower is designed with four tiers, each of which has a ping pong ball sitting on a track. The balls roll around when cats swat at it, and the tower’s non-slip base keeps it sturdy during play. Best tunnel Tunnels aren’t exactly toys, but they’re essential for play time, experts told us. Cats run through and hide inside them before pouncing on toys. I also throw plushies and balls inside my cats’ tunnel for them to chase. Feline Ruff’s 55-inch long tunnel has three arms and a peephole on the top. There’s a hanging jingle ball attachment for cats to swat at, too. Whenever my cats aren’t playing in their tunnel, they sleep inside it because the enclosed space makes them feel cozy and safe. How to shop for cat toys While shopping for cat toys, experts recommend thinking about the following factors. Toy type: Experts break cat toys down into categories like interactive, inanimate, puzzles and electric (read more about each toy type below). Keep a variety of toys available at home to make play interesting for cats and ensure they don’t get bored. Different toys also stimulate different natural instincts, like chasing, seeking, pouncing and exploring, says Gonzalez. If you buy an electric cat toy, remember that you’ll need to replace the batteries or recharge it every so often.Catnip: Catnip, a plant part of the mint family, tends to make cats feel happy when they smell it and mellow when they eat it, experts told us. You can buy toys that are stuffed or infused with catnip, as well as toys designed with a refillable pocket you can add dried catnip to.Safety: Cats are mischievous, so it’s always a good idea to monitor them while they’re playing with a new toy, says Van de Kieft. Make sure they don’t excessively chew on toys, especially those that have strings or yarn hanging off them. Also be extra cautious about toys that have small, detachable parts or elastic bands. These items are choking hazards and could cause internal blockages if ingested, says Gonzalez. Are laser toys bad for cats? “Laser toys are the worst toys for cats,” says Van de Kieft. In fact, studies show that there’s a high correlation between cats who frequently play with laser toys and behaviors consistent with obsessive compulsive disorder. “Cats are tactile, and when they can’t grab anything, they get frustrated,” says Grossmann. Overall, all the experts I spoke to recommend against letting your cat play with laser pointers. But if you decide to use them, make sure your cat tosses around a tangible toy afterward to feel some sense of capture, which can help prevent frustration and obsessive behavior to some degree, says Gonzalez. What are the best types of toys for cats? Understanding the different types of cat toys available can help you buy a handful that yours will love. Here’s how our experts break down cat toys: Interactive toys are those that require pet owners’ involvement in play time. Examples include wand toys and teaser toys — pet owners hold the toy’s handle while cats play with the ribbon or prey attachment.Inanimate toys are those that cats can play with themselves by kicking, chasing and swatting. Examples include plush toys like mice, as well as balls, springs and kicker toys. You can also throw inanimate toys to your cat for them to run after, or hide them around your home, creating a hide and seek game.Electric toys are rechargeable or battery-operated, and they engage cats by automatically moving. They’re not a substitute for interactive toys, but they can add extra entertainment and enrichment to cats’ days. Electronic toys are especially great for high energy cats who need more frequent play sessions, as well as people with busy schedules. However, they move in patterns cats eventually pick up on, making the toys predictable and boring, says Grossmann. That’s why it’s best to use electronic toys once in a while — if cats only play with them occasionally, it takes them longer to pick up on movement patterns so the toy remains interesting.Tunnels are toy-adjacent — they’re not exactly toys the same way catnip-filled plushies are, but they are essential for play, says Van de Kieft, who recommends that all cat owners have at least one. “Tunnels create safe places to hide and rest, but they’re also fun for play time,” she says. Puzzle feeders are mentally stimulating brain games for cats that bring out their hunting and foraging instincts, says Van de Kieft. They force cats to work for their food, which is what they’d be doing in the wild. And when cats finally get to their treat, they feel good about themselves, so it’s a confidence boosting activity, too. Each puzzle feeder has a difficulty level rated on a scale from 1 to 4 (1 being the easiest and 4 being the most difficult). Dog puzzle feeders tend to be more challenging, so if your cat is breezing through a level 4 puzzle, consider buying a higher level dog puzzle. As an alternative to puzzle feeders, you can hide treats around your home, creating a scavenger hunt for your cat. We also take steps to ensure that all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and with no undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Dr. Abel Gonzalez is a veterinarian and the clinical director at Dutch, a pet telehealth company.Jennifer Van de Kieft is a certified advanced feline training and behavior professional. She owns Cat Advocate, a feline behavior consulting company.Sandra Grossmann is the owner of The Feline Consultant LLC, offering cat behavior and nutrition consultations for cats. For this article, I interviewed three experts about how to shop for cat toys and rounded up NBC Selected staff favorite products. I also have two cats, and have raised a total of six cats throughout my lifetime. I’ve volunteered at animal shelters for over a decade as well. articles.title: Harassed over friend’s unpaid loan, Maharashtra man kills him
articles.summary: Panvel man arrested for murdering friend after harassment from loan recovery calls over unpaid EMI; body and weapon recovered, custody till Nov 21.
articles.body: NAVI MUMBAI: Allegedly fed up with calls for loan recovery after his friend defaulted on his EMI payments, a 30-year-old man allegedly murdered him and dumped his body in an isolated area in Panvel over a week ago. He was arrested on Monday.Bala Kumbhar, senior inspector, Panvel city police, said Pratik Dilip Ambavale (23) from Thane bought a mobile on EMI for Rs 50,000 and gave the phone number of his friend, Pratik Mohan Jadhav, who lived in Panvel taluka, as his alternative contact number. But he defaulted on the EMIs and Jadhav began getting calls daily from a loan recovery agent.Jadhav asked Ambavale to meet him on Nov 7 in Panvel. The two consumed liquor at an isolated spot and had an argument over the loan recovery calls, said Kumbhar. Ambavale allegedly kicked Jadhav, who retaliated by stabbing him multiple times in the abdomen with a knife. Jadhav then dumped him in nearby bushes and fled.Ambavale’s family filed a missing person complaint on Nov 9. The corpse and the murder weapon have been recovered. articles.title: Erewhon’s absurd Thanksgiving dinner takeout for $749 doesn’t even include cranberry sauce
articles.summary: You expected less from the home of the $20 strawberry?
articles.body:
Don't forget to bring your silver spoon.

Ultra-luxe California grocer Erewhon is selling the "ultimate" Thanksgiving takeout dinner for a cool $749. Available to purchase for delivery on the grocer's website , the pricey meal is intended to serve 8 to 10 people.

The feast comes complete with a large free-range cooked turkey, roasted vegetable stuffing, roasted rainbow carrots, Brussels sprouts, garlic mashed potatoes, turkey gravy, and a deep dish pumpkin pie — but you'll have to buy cranberry sauce separately.

"Erewhon's Ultimate Feast presents a complete holiday meal," the grocer's website reads. "This thoughtfully curated selection brings together traditional holiday elements in one comprehensive offering."

The chain is also offering a more budget-conscious version of the feast for $439, which serves 4 to six people, as well as a vegan option priced at $340, also serving 4 to 6. That omes with turmeric lasagna, green beans with almonds, wild rice stuffing, Brussels sprouts, yam purée, and pumpkin pie.

With 14 locations across Southern California, Erewhon is infamous for its pricey exclusive items. Most notably, the grocer sells smoothies in the $20 range , and has gone viral for limited-time novelty products including a single strawberry sold for $20 and a $12 cup of "sacred water."

If you're looking for a more affordable ready-made Thanksgiving meal, Aldi's Thanksgiving feast goes for just $39 and serves 10.

The pocket-friendly meal includes a 16-pound turkey, stuffing, sweet potatoes, Hawaiian sweet rolls, cranberries, peas, carrots, celery, pumpkin pie ingredients, milk and whipping cream.

"Thanksgiving shouldn't require a calculator or a coupon strategy," Aldi CEO Atty McGrath said in a news release. "At ALDI, shoppers can put a 16-pound turkey and the Thanksgiving classics on the table for 10 people, all for under $39. No hoops. Just a really good meal at a really good price."

Ready-made meals may be attractive to shoppers this year as the cost of hosting Thanksgiving rises. According to a new survey from LendingTree , Americans hosting Thanksgiving this year expect to spend an average of $427 on food, drinks, and housewares, a 3% increase from last year.

The survey also revealed that 51% of Americans are considering hosting Thanksgiving this year, down from 59% last year.

The cost of food itself is also up, with grocery prices increasing 0.4% in October, and 'food away from home' (restaurants and fast food) prices increasing 0.5%, according to the Consumer Price Index .

articles.title: Uncontacted Indigenous tribe reaches out for help in the Brazilian Amazon
articles.summary: Only around 300 members of the Awá people are left.
articles.body:
Around the world, the number of uncontacted Indigenous tribes continues to dwindle. Indigenous rights advocates estimate that half of the nearly 200 communities still existing in comparative isolation could disappear within a decade , without proper safeguards against climate change , land loss, fame-seeking opportunists , and illegal industrial encroachments. Unfortunately, the situation has apparently grown so dire that some Indigenous groups are reaching out for help—and exposing themselves to potentially deadly foreign diseases in the process.

On November 17, the nonprofit advocacy group Survival International reported a recent incident in which 20 members of the Awá people intentionally contacted local government officials in the Brazilian Amazon. Although proficient hunter-gatherers, the group requested yams before taking them back into the rainforest.

"This is a troubling indication of how the continued invasion of uncontacted peoples' forests puts otherwise self-sufficient Indigenous people in real danger," Survival International director Caroline Pearce said in a statement .

The Awá are one of the world's last uncontacted Indigenous tribes, whose ties to the Brazilian rainforest stretch back centuries. They faced their first attacks from European settlers during the 1800s, which eventually forced them to adopt a nomadic lifestyle to avoid future encounters. Brazil finally supplied the Awá with settlement areas during the mid-1980s, but it still took years before the government properly invested in demarcated land. In the meantime, numerous deadly interactions with loggers, farmers, and other illegal intruders had reduced the Awá community to barely 300 people. Of those, advocates estimate only about one-third of the hunter-gatherers remain completely isolated from the outside world.

"The Brazilian government must commit the resources necessary to protect [the region of] Arariboia from the loggers and ranchers who are razing it, in flagrant defiance of the law," Pearce added.

In addition to the advocacy work by Survival International, the Awá are supported by a team of Indigenous members of the Guajajara community known as the Forest Guardians . These volunteers have spent years pushing back against illegal cattle ranchers and loggers attempting to claim land in Arariboia, often dying as a result of their efforts.

"The Forest Guardians have always worked to protect the Awá against encroachment, even at the cost of losing warriors in battle," the organization said. "We demand immediate action from the relevant authorities…to ensure what the Awá believe is best for them, safeguarding their lives, health, safety and dignity. FOR THE AWÁ, FOR THE TENETEHAR [language], AND FOR THE FOREST!"

articles.title: Europe assassination scheme emerges as Iran denies DC 'dirty bomb' plot amid Trump warning
articles.summary: President Donald Trump warned Iran would pay a price like no other as Tehran's deputy foreign minister called the chemical weapons report a "shameful lie."
articles.body: Iran on Tuesday slammed allegations that it was plotting a chemical weapons attack in Washington, D.C., calling the claims a "shameful lie" within hours of President Donald Trump warning that Tehran would face unprecedented retaliation if it ever targeted the nation's capital. Tehran's denial followed a CNN report that U.S. intelligence agencies had uncovered Iranian plans for potential attacks on senior administration officials, including the possible use of chemical weapons or a radioactive "dirty bomb." The allegations also emerged amid reports of a separate Iranian-linked assassination plot targeting an Israeli executive in Greece and with Israeli security officials believing Tehran aims to target Israelis overseas as the war continues, according to news outlet Ynet Global. Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs Kazem Gharibabadi immediately rejected the allegations in a post on X, invoking Iran's history as a victim of chemical warfare. TRUMP WARNS US WOULD 'DECIMATE AND DESTROY' IRAN OVER ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT "CNN's claim that Iran plans to use chemical weapons in Washington is a shameful lie and a distortion of history," Gharibabadi wrote. Trump was asked by reporters Tuesday during the first leg of his trip across Asia about the alleged plot against administration officials and if there was an imminent threat to D.C. "Well, if there is, they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before," Trump said. "I hope it's not, but ... we take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy. But this is why they can't have a nuclear weapon, by the way, in case people had any questions." SENIOR US OFFICIAL UNDERCUTS CNN'S ALARMING IRAN ‘DIRTY BOMB’ REPORT: ‘IT’S NOT NEW' "Iran is one of the biggest victims of chemical weapons; victims who were targeted with these inhumane weapons with the support of today's accusers, especially the United States," he added. "The truth must not become a casualty of the propaganda war," Gharibabadi warned. TRUMP ADMIN THREATENS IRAN WITH 'CONSEQUENCES' AS ALLIES CONVENE AMID THREATS OF POST-ELECTION ESCALATION CNN reported, citing seven officials familiar with the intelligence, that American agencies had detected Iranian efforts to develop potential attack options against senior administration officials in Washington. White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said the administration was monitoring potential threats, but that "at this time, there are no credible threats to the homeland." IRAN COULD MOVE SHADOW WAR IN A DANGEROUS DIRECTION, EXPERTS WARN ON BACK OF TWO POSSIBLE TERROR ATTACKS Meanwhile, Israeli intelligence reportedly helped foil a separate alleged Iranian-linked assassination plot Tuesday targeting an Israeli executive in Greece, leading to five arrests in Greece and North Macedonia, according to Ynet. Citing sources, the outlet reported that Mossad gave intelligence to Greek and North Macedonian authorities as part of a joint effort to disrupt the plot. North Macedonia's National Security Agency announced that authorities had uncovered the plan, with one North Macedonian national arrested in Greece last Thursday and extradited to his home country. Four others were said to have been detained in Skopje, North Macedonia. The alleged plot was directed by Iranian national Edris Jahangiri Mavaneh, whom the agency linked to people associated with Iranian intelligence and security services, including alleged drug trafficker Naji Sharifi Zindashti, according to Ynet. IRAN TRIED TO ASSASSINATE ONE OF NETANYAHU'S SONS, PRIME MINISTER SAYS Zindashti is also wanted by the FBI for operating a network that targets Iranian activists and dissidents abroad. According to the bureau, Zindashti used encrypted, Internet-based messaging applications to hire criminal elements within North America and to murder two individuals who fled Iran. Greek outlet Kathimerini meanwhile, also reported that the suspects allegedly planned to assassinate a senior Israeli executive working for a company operating in Greece. North Macedonia's security agency said investigators also uncovered secret meetings involving suspects in several countries, including Iran. According to Ynet, Israeli security officials said Tehran considers its war with Israel as unresolved and is looking for opportunities to retaliate through attacks beyond the Middle East region.

articles.title: All these tech outages all at once
articles.summary: A series of high-profile glitches impacting office software, flights and banking are spiking concerns about tech vulnerabilities.
articles.body: Welcome to the daily Inside Scoop newsletter. Rely on Microsoft cloud products? Had a flight on Friday? Needed to bank at Chase? articles.title: Man legally named Captain America charged with murder after allegedly giving victim’s girlfriend chilling note
articles.summary: A man legally named Captain America allegedly gave a woman a note saying her boyfriend was dead and demanding her money. Police later found the boyfriend dead inside a home.
articles.body: An Illinois woman giving her boyfriend’s co-worker a ride escaped after he allegedly handed her a chilling note saying her boyfriend was dead and demanding all her money. Police then went to check on her boyfriend and found his body inside a Peoria home. The passenger, Captain C. America, 34, was charged with first-degree murder in the death of Khanh Dinh, 63, according to Peoria County State’s Attorney Jodi M. Hoos’ office. COWORKER ACCUSED OF SLASHING WOMAN’S THROAT DURING RIDE HOME, VICTIM ESCAPED MOVING CAR: POLICE The encounter unfolded Friday, Nov. 13, when the woman was driving America, whom she knew because he worked with Dinh, prosecutors said. "While in the car, the defendant handed her a note that said her boyfriend was dead and demanded all of her money," Hoos’ office said. SUSPECT IN CUSTODY FOR ALLEGED MURDER OF COLLEGE STUDENT AFTER POLICE RELEASED EERIE SURVEILLANCE PHOTOS The woman managed to get away and call police in neighboring Tazewell County. Officers tracked down America and took him into custody shortly afterward, prosecutors said. When officers removed him from a squad car, they found the note the woman had described. GYPSY ROSE BLANCHARD’S PARTNER, KEN URKER, FOUND DEAD INSIDE HIS LOUISIANA HOME: SHERIFF The woman's account led Peoria officers to a home on North Sheridan Road, where they arrived for a welfare check at about 7:14 p.m., police said. Inside, they found Dinh dead. A preliminary autopsy indicated he died from blunt-force head trauma, according to prosecutors. Hoos’ office announced the murder charge Monday. Authorities have not publicly identified a motive in statements released about the case. America, whose full legal name is Captain Cautious America, was previously known as Mark Anderson. He changed his name about a decade ago because he hoped to run for political office and wanted to stand out on the ballot, according to The Peoria Journal Star. America remains in the Tazewell County Jail, where Peoria police said he was being held on unrelated charges. A Nov. 14 jail booking entry lists an unlawful restraint charge. articles.summary: Waymo will stop putting its driverless vehicles on U.S. freeways for now.
articles.body: Waymo will stop putting its driverless vehicles on U.S. freeways for now. The move comes after California banned the company’s robotaxis from state highways after officials determined that they pose an “imminent hazard to public safety.” “We’ve proactively implemented a freeway operating restriction across all of our markets,” a Waymo spokesperson said Tuesday in a statement. “Notably, this only extends to our freeway service, and we’re working to quickly and safely re-open freeway routing.” California’s Department of Motor Vehicles said it issued its ban Nov. 11 after one of Waymo’s autonomous vehicles tried to pass highway patrol officers conducting a traffic break on a San Francisco-area freeway this month. The department also cited a separate incident in which three of the company’s vehicles entered an active construction closure on another San Francisco-area highway. “The Department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present,” the department said. Similar restrictions were placed on the company after similar incidents earlier this year, the department said. The ban will remain in place until Waymo can address the issue, according to the release. In a statement, Waymo pointed out that the construction zone incidents did not involve injuries or collisions and said it is complying with the restrictions. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said it is in communication with both the state DMV and Waymo and will “take additional actions as appropriate.” Waymo’s robotaxis are in more than a dozen cities across the U.S. Waymo, which is owned by Google’s parent company, Alphabet Inc., first introduced the driverless taxis in San Francisco in 2024. Waymo said it is working with state officials to “diligently and responsibly” resume freeway operations and service continues to operate normally on regular ground-level roads.

articles.title: COP31: Pakistan's solar revolution has been so successful the national grid is lagging behind
articles.summary: People installing their own solar panels has helped boost the solar share of Pakistan's electricity from 1% to 28%.
articles.body:
Jewellery, glimmering silverware, sofas and an air-conditioning unit. Three months after his wedding, Faisal Shahzad's home in rural Punjab is bursting with gifts from his bride's family, as part of the dowry.

But the most prized possession is tucked under the bed: a 340W solar panel.

"In the summer we ran it from 08:00 in the morning until the evening," he says, adding they didn't need to use grid power at all during the day. "We ran our air cooler on it all day."

Pakistan has seen a boom in imported solar panels, which glisten from the rooftops of homes and hospitals; from farmers' fields to industrial complexes.

From 2018 to 2025, the share of electricity generated from solar energy in the country rose from 1% to 28%, according to Pakistan-based think tank Renewables First, with some seven million households now owning panels.

People used to gift motorbikes or other household items at weddings, Shahzad says. "Now they give a solar panel and an air cooler. It has almost become a must."

Alongside the solar panel he still uses the national grid to meet his energy needs, particularly as he lives in a house with his family and brothers' families, who often use multiple appliances simultaneously. But in a country where the average wage is just under 40,000 Pakistani rupees (£110; $145) per month, bills are becoming unaffordable, rising to 15,000-18,000 rupees.

This year, COP31 is pushing the world to move away from fossil-powered vehicles, boilers and other greenhouse gas-emitting equipment. And while Pakistan has become a poster child for solarisation, the national grid system is experiencing knock-on eﬀects.

The big pivot to solar wasn't driven by government policy but by individual Pakistani households. Most people we spoke to said they installed panels to escape soaring electricity prices from an often unreliable national grid.

Electricity tariffs have more than doubled in a few years, says Muhammad Hassan Dajana, industry liaison at Renewables First, while the cost of Chinese solar panels has "decreased by 93%".

"People have just found another way to be able to survive," says Energy Minister Awais Ahmad Leghari. "It's a very healthy thing. We have adapted to the situation. The people have reacted and responded in a very economically viable and efficient manner."

While the solar boom brings clear benefits, particularly for a country that imports huge amounts of fuel, there are worries too.

Pakistan needs to avoid the so-called utility death spiral.

When people buy less energy from the national grid, fewer customers are left to cover the fixed costs of maintaining it. That can force prices up - which in turn encourages even more people to switch to solar.

Over time, this can lead to a two-tier system in which those who can't afford to buy panels face ever-rising bills, while the national grid becomes an increasing burden on the state.

"You'll have a white elephant in the form of a state-owned enterprise that requires a lot of public funding to just stay afloat," says Dajana.

Pakistan's government says the costs are already being felt.

"In just the past two years, the exodus from the grid has cost the rest of the consumers more than $500 million [£378m] a year," says Leghari. "That's a very big burden."

The government doesn't want to pull people away from solar, he explains, but wants the grid to be more competitive to be able to offer better energy prices.

Private power producers, which feed into the grid, have been heavily criticised inside Pakistan for locking the country into costly, inflexible contracts. Producers themselves point to broader structural problems like poor grid maintenance as contributing to higher bills. Leghari says the government has renegotiated most of the contracts and is now focused on making the grid more efficient with better storage, less waste and more innovation.

Leghari wants the country to run on "up to 90% clean power" by the end of 2036 - including renewables and nuclear - with dependence on imported energy reducing from 26% to 4%.

But as the government tries to improve the grid, solar is still expanding with widespread adoption in industry.

Kohinoor Textiles Mills in Islamabad, which is powered by a sea of huge blue solar panels, is one example. Utilities manager Sabawoon Khan describes them as his "baby", pointing at construction work levelling the ground for more panels.

When the sun shines, the mills' hundreds of machines are powered entirely by solar energy, Khan says. The heavy-furnace-oil engines they once relied on sit mothballed in a warehouse.

But there are limits. When it's too cloudy or polluted, and during the night, the company takes more energy from the national grid. In the coming weeks, like other firms, it will start using industrial batteries which can store excess solar energy.

"We needed to reduce our energy costs and this was one way to do it," says Taufique Sayeed Saigol, the mills' CEO, who adds the plan is not to disconnect from the grid altogether.

"The state unfortunately doesn't have the resources so we can't really say that we blame everything on the state. We do some of the things ourselves."

Critics accuse the government of moving the goalposts on solar power. Previously, households could feed excess electricity into the grid and earn credits, which were then used to offset the cost of grid power when the sun wasn't shining. That policy changed earlier this year.

"Initially their policy was very helpful," says Arif Ehsan Malik, president of Faisalabad's chamber of commerce. "But then the policy changed. Now they have started purchasing at a lower rate and selling back at a higher rate."

Malik says that makes a big difference for small and medium businesses. Leghari counters that the costs of the initial model didn't add up; the electricity the solar producers put into the system was much cheaper than the electricity they ended up taking out of it.

"Those profits were coming at the cost of the rest of the consumers of the grid. Had we not changed those regulations, the rest of the consumers would have been burdened by at least 150 to 200 billion rupees a year, say, two years from now."

Despite admitting that the first wave of solar adoption was a "surprise" to the government, Leghari says he has no fear that solar could outrun their plans, saying it has been incorporated into their 10-year forecasts and the numbers leaving the grid have slowed.

Pakistan has big ambitions for solar; there are plans to open solar battery factories around the country and encourage more electric vehicles.

"There are two paths ahead," Dajana says. One is a future where solar and the grid work in parallel, demonstrating how a gradual energy transition can succeed. The other is where Pakistan becomes a cautionary tale, burdened with a costly, declining grid.

Shahzad's solar ambitions for his home in rural Punjab certainly have not slowed.

"We plan to get another 10-15 panels and install them on the roof, then connect a full system with batteries and back up.

"The plan is to be fully self-sufficient."

articles.title: Trump pede US$ 50 bilhões para aviação dos EUA, mas sofre resistência | G1
articles.standfirst: Adversários e até mesmo integrantes do partido do presidente Donald Trump afirmam publicamente que não apoiam o pedido. Medida pretende reformar o controle do tráfego aéreo depois do apagão geral na sexta-feira (13).
articles.summary: Trump pede US$ 50 bilhões para reformar a aviação após apagão aéreo nos EUA, mas enfrenta resistência até de republicanos que exigem foco apenas em segurança.
articles.body:
Passageiros aguardam na fila de segurança do Aeroporto Nacional Ronald Reagan, próximo a Washington, após a retomada das decolagens nos EUA, neste sábado (14). — Foto: Reuters

Senadores republicanos afirmaram nesta terça-feira (17) que não apoiariam o pedido do governo do presidente Donald Trump de US$ 50 bilhões (R$ cerca de 290 bilhões) para reformas no controle de tráfego aéreo e melhorias nos aeroportos, mas estão dispostos a apoiar um pedido mais limitado e voltado para a segurança.

O secretário de Transportes do governo Trump, Sean Duffy, havia solicitado na sexta-feira US$ 30 bilhões (R$ 173 milhões) — incluindo US$ 18 bilhões (R$ 104 milhões) para aeroportos —, mas elevou esse valor para os US$ 50 bilhões (R$ cerca de 290 bilhões) pedidos agora depois da paralisação nacional dos voos, atribuída a um único roteador, resultou no cancelamento de mais de 18 mil voos.

“Vou aceitar o que conseguir e vou trabalhar com o Congresso para garantir que as mais altas prioridades sejam atendidas primeiro”, disse Duffy em uma coletiva de imprensa, após um almoço semanal de discussão de políticas com senadores republicanos. “Vou trabalhar com o que quer que eles me deem.”

O Congresso americano aprovou no ano passado US$12,5 bilhões (R$ 72 bilhões), e apenas cerca de 30% foram gastos, segundo os senadores. Duffy enfrentou algumas perguntas hostis de senadores republicanos durante o almoço, que questionaram o custo da medida, segundo assessores do Senado.

Os democratas afirmam que querem mais respostas sobre o que deu errado na sexta-feira antes de aprovarem mais recursos.

Alguns republicanos também disseram que as companhias aéreas ou outros usuários do sistema deveriam arcar com parte dos custos da modernização. “Não vou votar a favor de fornecer dinheiro a eles para ajudar os aeroportos locais”, disse o senador republicano John Kennedy, afirmando que foi um “enorme erro” passar de US$30 bilhões para US$50 bilhões.

A iniciativa ocorre dias depois de o país sofrer um apagão aéreo generalizado, que forçou o fechamento de todos os aeroportos do país e interrupção de poucos e decolagens por mais de quatro horas na sexta-feira (13).

Uma falha de comunicação fez com que a Agência de Aviação dos Estados Unidos (FAA, na sigla em inglês) tomasse a medida extrema e rara — a segunda desde o 11 de setembro de 2001. Nesta terça-feira (17), a agência suspendeu a instalação de roteadores que levaram à paralisação de voos no país.

O governo Trump, no entanto, afirmou que a culpa da falha é da gestão anterior, do governo de Joe Biden . Segundo o atual presidente, o caso foi "um desastre" e que a gestão da aviação durante o governo do democrata Joe Biden comprometeu o funcionamento, o que acarretou na falha.

"Tudo em que eles tocaram deu errado", escreveu o presidente republicano na plataforma Truth Social.

Trump, no entanto, enfrenta problemas dentro do próprio partido para defender o investimento após o caos aéreo. O senador republicano Rick Scott, por exemplo disse acreditar que são necessários mais US$10 bilhões para consertar os sistemas de controle de tráfego aéreo.

“O Congresso tem um papel a desempenhar, mas as companhias aéreas precisam contribuir financeiramente e também se comprometer com isso. E sim, elas podem fazer isso sem aumentar os preços das passagens”, disse Scott.

O líder da maioria no Senado, John Thune, disse que os republicanos fizeram perguntas sobre o valor de US$50 bilhões e mencionaram a solicitação anterior de US$30 bilhões. “Vamos ver o que o tráfego aguentar, o que é viável”, disse Thune.

Já o presidente da Comissão de Comércio do Senado, Ted Cruz, disse que esperava que mais recursos para melhorias relacionadas à segurança fossem financiados, mas afirmou que a mensagem do Congresso no ano passado foi: "demonstrem que vocês realmente podem modernizar e voltem ao Congresso quando precisarem de recursos adicionais".

articles.title: Xi Jinping e Putin criticam o Ocidente antes de encontro com Trump | G1
articles.standfirst: Chinês atacou protecionismo, enquanto russo disse que sanções perderam poder de intimidação.
articles.summary: Na cúpula da APEC, Xi Jinping e Putin condenam sanções e o protecionismo antes de reunião decisiva com Donald Trump sobre conflitos globais e comércio internacional.
articles.body:
Xi e Putin na Cúpula da Cooperação Econômica Ásia-Pacífico (APEC) 2026. — Foto: Sputnik/Vyacheslav Prokofyev/Pool via REUTERS

O presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, prometeu nesta quarta-feira (18) combater o protecionismo comercial, enquanto seu homólogo russo, Vladimir Putin, criticou as sanções ocidentais. Os dois preparam o terreno para uma reunião trilateral de alto risco com Donald Trump.

Eles fizeram seus discursos em uma cúpula da Cooperação Econômica Ásia-Pacífico (APEC) no polo tecnológico de Shenzhen , no sul da China , antes da chegada do presidente dos EUA, Trump, vindo de Manila, onde ele se reunia com importantes aliados regionais .

Os três homens devem se encontrar à margem do evento na quinta-feira (19) e possivelmente discutir a guerra da Rússia com a Ucrânia e a guerra dos EUA no Irã, bem como outros pontos críticos, como comércio, inteligência artificial e armas nucleares.

O encontro foi comparado à Conferência de Yalta de 1945 entre os EUA, a Grã-Bretanha e a União Soviética, que formalizou as esferas de influência, preparou o terreno para a ordem pós-Segunda Guerra Mundial e se tornou uma referência abreviada aos acordos das grandes potências impostos a países menores.

Isso também deixou apreensivos os líderes de economias menores, particularmente na Europa e na Ásia, que temem que as maiores potências militares do mundo ignorem seus interesses.

Em seu discurso de abertura, Xi Jinping pediu apoio ao que chamou de "comércio livre e aberto", tentando retratar seu país como um parceiro estável no cenário global, em contraste com seu principal rival econômico, os Estados Unidos, que aumentaram as tarifas e adotaram uma política externa mais agressiva sob o governo Trump.

A mensagem encontra ressonância no Sul Global

As declarações de Xi surgiram após Washington anunciar novas restrições ao acesso da China a chips de IA avançados de empresas como a Nvidia (NVDA.O) , o que pode complicar ainda mais a frágil trégua comercial com Pequim. A China prometeu retaliar.

"Devemos defender firmemente o sistema multilateral de comércio baseado em regras, com a Organização Mundial do Comércio como seu núcleo, apoiar o comércio e o investimento livres e abertos, e manter a estabilidade e o bom funcionamento das cadeias industriais e de suprimentos globais", disse Xi a uma plateia de executivos de empresas.

Os parceiros comerciais ocidentais criticaram a China por apresentar superávits comerciais anuais superiores a 1 trilhão de dólares, por meio de políticas que apoiam seu setor manufatureiro em detrimento de seus consumidores.

Pequim afirma que seu modelo de crescimento é adequado para uma economia que ainda está se aproximando das mais ricas do mundo, mas Washington, Bruxelas e outros estão preocupados com o domínio da China na cadeia de suprimentos, que confere ao país influência geopolítica, e dizem que suas políticas ameaçam suas indústrias e empregos.

Arte coloca Trump, Putin e Xi em uma referência à conferência de Yalta, de 1945 — Foto: REUTERS/Alexey Pavlishak

Xi Jinping afirmou que a China continuará investindo em seu complexo industrial e desenvolvendo novas tecnologias que também beneficiarão outros países. A segunda maior economia do mundo reduzirá as tarifas e abrirá ainda mais seus mercados, ao mesmo tempo em que se opõe ao protecionismo e ao unilateralismo, acrescentou.

"Sua mensagem provavelmente terá repercussão em muitos países do Sul Global e reforça o esforço de Pequim em contrastar sua estratégia tecnológica com a de Washington", disse George Chen, sócio e presidente da área digital do The Asia Group.

A viagem de Trump à Ásia é a primeira desde a derrota do seu Partido Republicano nas eleições de meio de mandato, enquanto as alegações envolvendo o fundador da Nvidia, Jensen Huang, e um suposto espião chinês aumentam a tensão.

Ainda assim, a maioria dos analistas espera que Washington e Pequim mantenham relações relativamente estáveis, visto que Trump e Xi devem se encontrar novamente este ano, após a reunião de quinta-feira em Shenzhen, na conferência do G20 em Miami, em dezembro.

Putin, que discursava após a Ucrânia ter destruído a vital ponte rodoviária de Kerch, que liga a Crimeia à Rússia, num duro golpe para a sua guerra de quatro anos, seguiu-se a Xi no palco com um discurso que descreveu as potências ocidentais como "ex-hegemonias".

Ele afirmou que a Europa estava em um "declínio humilhante" e que as sanções anti-Rússia impostas após a invasão da Ucrânia tiveram o efeito contrário, fortalecendo, ao contrário, seu país.

"A experiência demonstrou que as ferramentas tradicionais de domínio econômico e coerção de fato já cumpriram seu papel, tendo perdido grande parte de seu poder de intimidação", disse Putin.

"Embora sanções, tarifas e restrições à exportação ainda possam exercer um certo efeito dissuasor, são incapazes de deter o crescimento — muito menos de destruir as economias dos concorrentes."

O Kremlin rejeitou esta semana as comparações com a Conferência de Yalta, classificando-as como "jogos de cientistas políticos", mas afirmou que o encontro terá um grande impacto nos assuntos globais. Pequim declarou que a reunião trilateral tem "significado inovador" e promoverá a paz mundial.

Trump também mencionou a possibilidade de se encontrar com o líder norte-coreano Kim Jong Un, mas isso ainda não foi confirmado.

Na terça-feira, Taiwan e Japão alertaram para incursões de aeronaves russas em seu espaço aéreo.

Putin descreveu o mundo como "turbulento" e "marcado por uma economia global fragmentada e crescentes riscos político-militares", mas afirmou que as divergências entre os países podem ser resolvidas "sentar à mesa de negociações".

"Portanto, espero um grande benefício potencial da próxima reunião trilateral entre os líderes da Rússia, China e Estados Unidos", disse ele.

articles.title: Inteligência artificial identifica se o Queijo Minas é verdadeiro | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa do IFMG, em Bambuí, usa imagens para identificar a origem do Queijo Minas Artesanal. Dois aplicativos estão em desenvolvimento para auxiliar produtores, consumidores e órgãos de inspeção.
articles.summary: A inteligência artificial desenvolvida pelo IFMG Bambuí usa um banco de imagens para verificar a origem do Queijo Minas Artesanal e combater fraudes no mercado.
articles.body:
As telas do aplicativo mostram o resultado da análise: de um lado um queijo verdadeiro e do outro, um queijo falsificado — Foto: reprodução/Aplicativo de Inspeção

É queijo da Canastra mesmo ou só parece? Pesquisadores do Instituto Federal de Minas Gerais ( IFMG ), campus Bambuí , no Centro-Oeste do estado, estão desenvolvendo um sistema que usa inteligência artificial (IA) para identificar a origem do Queijo Minas Artesanal e ajudar a combater falsificações.

A tecnologia funciona a partir de um banco de imagens de queijos produzidos em diferentes regiões de Minas Gerais. Com essas fotografias, a inteligência artificial é treinada para reconhecer as características dos produtos e identificar possíveis diferenças entre um queijo autêntico e outro vendido com uma origem que não corresponde à verdadeira.

Dois aplicativos fazem parte do projeto: um voltado para o cadastro dos queijos pelos produtores e outro para a verificação da autenticidade por consumidores e órgãos de inspeção. A proposta é que, no futuro, uma pessoa possa fotografar um queijo e consultar pelo celular se ele apresenta as características da região de origem informada.

O sistema ainda não está disponível ao público, mas um protótipo já foi desenvolvido e apresentou resultados positivos em testes com queijos da Serra da Canastra . Agora, os pesquisadores trabalham para ampliar o banco de imagens e incluir outras regiões produtoras, como Serro e Araxá.

Devido ao caráter inovador da pesquisa, a equipe também prepara um pedido de patente da tecnologia .

Da Serra da Canastra para a inteligência artificial

A ideia de usar a tecnologia para proteger a origem do Queijo Minas Artesanal surgiu durante a pandemia, quando o engenheiro eletricista Calebe Giaculi Júnior, um dos pesquisadores responsáveis pelo projeto, morou na Serra da Canastra.

Nesse período, ele teve contato com produtores e queijarias da região e percebeu que a tecnologia poderia ajudar a organizar informações sobre a produção e proteger a identidade dos queijos artesanais.

“Eu resolvi começar a levar os projetos que a gente estava desenvolvendo para esse novo ambiente que eu estava frequentando. E eu vi que a cadeia produtiva do Queijo Minas Artesanal, ela é muito carente de tecnologia”, contou Calebe.

A partir dessa experiência, os pesquisadores começaram a desenvolver um sistema capaz de reunir informações sobre os queijos e usar inteligência artificial para auxiliar na identificação da origem dos produtos.

O projeto prevê dois aplicativos que funcionam de forma complementar.

No aplicativo de cadastramento , os produtores poderão registrar informações sobre os queijos, como lote, data de produção e etiqueta, além de inserir fotografias dos produtos. Essas imagens irão alimentar um banco de dados usado para treinar a inteligência artificial.

👀➡️É como se o olhar atento do produtor, acostumado a reconhecer as características do próprio queijo, fosse incorporado a um sistema capaz de comparar imagens e identificar padrões.

Já o aplicativo de inspeção será voltado para consumidores e órgãos responsáveis pela fiscalização. A proposta é simples: fotografar um queijo, enviar a imagem ao aplicativo e receber uma análise feita pela IA.

🧀➡️O sistema irá comparar a fotografia com as imagens disponíveis no banco de dados e apresentar um resultado em percentual, indicando o grau de correspondência com as características dos queijos cadastrados.

Na prática, a tecnologia poderá ajudar a identificar possíveis falsificações de origem. Um exemplo é o queijo vendido como sendo da Canastra , mas que não apresenta as características dos produtos daquela região. O mesmo vale para queijos comercializados como sendo do Serro ou de outras regiões produtoras.

Consumidor pode fotografar os queijos e inserir a imagem no app para saber a procedência do alimento — Foto: Calebe Jr./Arquivo Pessoal

Para tornar a análise mais precisa, os pesquisadores pretendem reunir 150 mil imagens de queijos artesanais. A ideia é cruzar as fotografias cadastradas pelos produtores com aquelas enviadas pelos consumidores, ampliando a capacidade de identificação do sistema.

Mesmo com um banco de imagens menor, o protótipo já apresentou resultados positivos nos testes realizados com queijos da Canastra. A pesquisa agora avança para outras regiões produtoras certificadas de Minas Gerais.

Segundo Calebe, os resultados também mostraram que a tecnologia apresenta características inovadoras, o que levou a equipe a iniciar os preparativos para solicitar uma patente.

“A gente viu que essa tecnologia que a gente está desenvolvendo, ela tem um caráter único, então a gente consegue patentear. A gente viu que tinha algo novo e entrou com esse processo de pedir patente”, explicou o pesquisador.

Tecnologia poderá identificar outros produtos regionais

Embora o foco inicial seja o Queijo Minas Artesanal, os pesquisadores acreditam que a tecnologia poderá ser usada futuramente para verificar a autenticidade de outros alimentos ligados à identidade de determinadas regiões.

Entre os exemplos estão doces típicos de Araxá e produtos de charcutaria, como embutidos e carnes curadas, produzidos na Serra da Canastra.

“Por exemplo, se tem um doce que é típico da cidade de Araxá, da região de Araxá, o sistema no futuro pode ser usado. Hoje em dia está começando a ter muita charcutaria na região da Serra da Canastra [...] No futuro, o que a gente está fazendo com o queijo, vamos poder fazer com a charcutaria em breve”, afirmou Calebe.

Atualmente, o projeto busca recursos por meio de editais de incentivo à pesquisa para continuar o desenvolvimento da tecnologia.

Interessados em conhecer mais sobre o trabalho podem entrar em contato com o pesquisador Calebe Giaculi Júnior pelo telefone (34) 98889-6420 .

Queijo Minas Artesanal é patrimônio da humanidade

A pesquisa também busca contribuir para a valorização de um produto que faz parte da história e da cultura mineira.

Em 2024, os modos de fazer o Queijo Minas Artesanal foram reconhecidos como Patrimônio Cultural Imaterial da Humanidade pela Organização das Nações Unidas para a Educação, a Ciência e a Cultura (Unesco).

A tradição já era reconhecida como Patrimônio Cultural do Brasil pelo Instituto do Patrimônio Histórico e Artístico Nacional (Iphan) desde 2008.

articles.title: Lixo voador em Uberlândia: vídeo mostra lixo quase atingindo carro | G1
articles.standfirst: Motorista do veículo contou que estava voltando para casa quando foi surpreendido pelo lixo caindo do prédio. Prefeitura informou que vai notificar o síndico para identificação do morador infrator.
articles.summary: Após flagrante de lixo voador em Uberlândia, prefeitura notifica condomínio para identificar morador que arremessou fraldas e restos de comida sobre um veículo.
articles.body:
Uma câmera de segurança de um prédio do bairro Santa Mônica, em Uberlândia , no Triângulo Mineiro, registrou o momento em que lixo foi jogado do alto do condomínio e passou muito perto de um carro que trafegava pela rua Professor João Luís. O caso aconteceu na noite de sábado (14). Veja o vídeo acima.

Segundo o motorista, que não quis se identificar, ele voltava para casa com a esposa quando os dois foram surpreendidos pela queda dos detritos em frente ao prédio.

“Ao darmos conta do ocorrido, notamos que haviam lançado do prédio uma caixa com diversos tipos de resíduos, incluindo sacolas plásticas com restos de comida e fraldas usadas, os quais ficaram dispostos no meio da rua e quase atingiu nosso veículo. Essa é uma situação muito desagradável e não é a primeira vez que acontece. O lixo espalhado prejudica toda a vizinhança, bem como os funcionários coletores. Portanto, precisamos tratar desse assunto para que esse tipo de evento não ocorra e o autor seja identificado e punido dentro da legislação vigente”, relatou.

Moradores de prédios vizinhos reclamaram da situação em um grupo de mensagens. Um deles afirmou que chegou a mudar de bairro por causa de problemas desse tipo.

“Eu mudei de bairro por tamanha indignação de tudo que acontece e nunca teve solução para absolutamente nada”, contou.

Outro disse que saiu na rua no dia seguinte, no domingo (15), e viu o lixo espalhado.

“Eu fui andar com meus cachorros mais cedo e a rua estava uma carniça. Cheio de fralda suja, um nojo”, disse.

Em nota, a Secretaria Municipal de Serviços Urbanos (Sesurb) informou que o condomínio será notificado para que o síndico possa localizar o morador infrator. Leia a íntegra abaixo.

À TV Integração , o presidente da Comissão de Direito Urbanístico da Ordem dos Advogados do Brasil (OAB), Nelson Rezende de Toledo Piza, disse que, nessa situação, o morador que jogou o lixo pode ser responsabilizado.

"Na esfera Civil, se a pessoa atira um saco de lixo desses e atinge um pedestre ou um carro, pode ser buscada reparação. Dentro de condomínio também é importante que o síndico adote as medidas de acordo com o regulamento para que seja apurada essa responsabilização. A lei estipula pagamento de até cinco taxas condominiais para essa infração e em caso de recorrência, dez. Não sendo possível identificar quem é o real infrator, o próprio condomínio é condenado a ressarcir reparações", explicou.

"A Secretaria Municipal de Serviços Urbanos (Sesurb) informa que o condomínio será notificado para que o síndico possa localizar o morador infrator e a partir daí as providências cabíveis possam ser adotadas. A pasta reforça ainda que denúncias como esta podem ser feitas e acompanhadas pelos canais oficiais, via Portal da Prefeitura, pela Interface do Serviço de Informação Municipal (SIM) e do Fale com o Governo: ou pelo telefone (34) 3239-2800."

articles.title: Voos cancelados nos EUA: governo ainda investiga falha em roteador | G1
articles.standfirst: Falha em roteador paralisou operações aéreas por quase cinco horas; autoridades conseguiram reproduzir o problema, mas ainda investigam sua origem.
articles.summary: Após 18 mil voos cancelados nos EUA, o secretário Sean Duffy confirmou que a FAA e o FBI ainda buscam a causa da pane em um roteador instalado no Arkansas.
articles.body:
Passageiros aguardam no Aeroporto Internacional Logan após a Administração Federal de Aviação dos EUA (FAA) emitir uma ordem nacional de suspensão de voos em solo "devido a circunstâncias extraordinárias e razões de segurança", na sequência de um relatório anterior da agência sobre graves problemas de comunicação no controle de tráfego aéreo, em East Boston, Massachusetts, EUA, 13 de novembro de 2026 — Foto: Brian Snyder / REUTERS

O secretário de Transportes dos Estados Unidos, Sean Duffy, afirmou nesta terça-feira (17) que ainda não foi determinada a causa principal da falha no roteador ocorrida na sexta-feira (13), que provocou uma paralisação da aviação em todo o país e o cancelamento de mais de 18 mil voos.

Duffy disse que ainda não está claro por que a instalação, pela L3Harris Technologies, de um roteador em uma instalação remota em El Dorado, no Arkansas, teve impacto tão grande sobre a rede a ponto de provocar uma interrupção de quase cinco horas nas operações aéreas, afetando centenas de milhares de passageiros.

“Conseguimos reproduzir o que aconteceu em El Dorado, mas ainda não temos clareza sobre a causa principal do ocorrido”, disse Duffy a jornalistas após uma reunião com senadores.

A substituição fazia parte de uma transição rotineira de fios de cobre para fibra óptica digital com o objetivo de modernizar os equipamentos. O chefe da FAA, Bryan Bedford, disse a jornalistas que não tinham fundamento as especulações de que inteligência artificial estaria envolvida na interrupção.

Duffy afirmou que a instalação de outros 68 roteadores, fabricados pela Juniper Networks, da Hewlett Packard Enterprise, não havia causado problemas. No entanto, disse que a FAA suspendeu as instalações de roteadores da Juniper enquanto os testes continuam em um laboratório da L3Harris na Flórida, com a presença da FAA, da Cisco e do FBI.

A L3Harris afirmou que está cooperando com a investigação oficial sobre o que deu errado.

Duffy disse que, durante o governo Biden, a FAA substituiu 19% de sua rede de telecomunicações, passando do cobre para a fibra óptica, enquanto, em um ano, o governo Trump substituiu pouco mais de 50%.

“Precisamos concluir esse trabalho. Caso contrário, permanecer no sistema antigo por mais tempo significará mais riscos”, afirmou.

A L3Harris vinha instalando roteadores da Juniper para substituir equipamentos da Cisco fabricados em 2001 e que deveriam ter sido trocados em 2006, segundo a FAA.

Duffy afirmou que a FAA passou um ano testando os roteadores da Juniper em seu centro de tecnologia, mas que a instalação no centro de comunicações por rádio do Arkansas provocou uma sobrecarga em um importante sistema de comunicações do governo. Isso desestabilizou as comunicações com aeronaves e os dados de radar, afetando 17 dos 22 centros de controle de tráfego aéreo em rota da FAA.

Após o incidente, a função de transmissão também foi desativada em todos os novos roteadores e em outros 60 equipamentos do sistema como medida de precaução, informou a FAA.

A HPE, proprietária da Juniper, afirmou acreditar que seus equipamentos estavam funcionando conforme configurados.

“A FAA está avaliando a configuração e o desempenho de toda a infraestrutura envolvida para determinar a causa”, afirmou a empresa.

articles.title: Pentagon detains senior US Army officer accused of spying for Russians after UK arrest
articles.summary: Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner was handed to U.S. military authorities after British counterterrorism police arrested him on suspicion of spying for Russia.
articles.body: A U.S. Army lieutenant colonel suspected of spying for Russia was handed over to U.S. military authorities Tuesday, days after British counterterrorism police arrested him on suspicion of violating national security laws. Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner, 41, was arrested Nov. 10 near Gloucester, England, on suspicion of assisting a foreign intelligence service and obtaining or disclosing protected information under the United Kingdom's National Security Act. British authorities previously said the allegations involved Russia, which the Kremlin denied any connection to. SENIOR US ARMY SOLDIER ARRESTED IN UK ON SUSPICION OF SPYING FOR RUSSIA The Associated Press, citing a U.S. official, reported that Tyner had not provided information to Russia. Tyner's transfer followed consultations between British prosecutors, the U.K. attorney general's office and U.S. authorities, according to London's Metropolitan Police. Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of U.K.'s Counter Terrorism Policing, said investigators referred the case to the Crown Prosecution Service, which consulted the attorney general's office and U.S. authorities before transferring the investigation. RUSSIAN SPIES ORCHESTRATED $40K MURDER PLOT IN NATION’S CAPITAL, US ALLEGES "These are extremely serious allegations, and our collective response should send a strong message that we will act swiftly and robustly where we suspect this kind of espionage activity taking place," Taylor said in a statement. FBI Director Kash Patel said the officer was in custody following a joint espionage investigation involving the FBI's Philadelphia field office, its London legal attaché office, British counterterrorism police, MI5, U.K. defense counterintelligence officials and U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command. "This FBI has zero tolerance for anyone who betrays their oath to the United States or puts our national security at risk. That’s been demonstrated by the 167 counterintelligence and espionage arrests we’ve made over the last 21 months, a 53% increase," Patel said. Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, commander of U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command, warned service members against violating their oath to defend the Constitution. "This case should serve as a stark warning to any service member suspected of violating the oath we all take to protect and defend the Constitution," Stinchon said. Tyner, who previously deployed to Afghanistan, Iraq and Qatar, served as a senior human resources officer with NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps at Imjin Barracks near Gloucester. The British-led multinational force, which includes personnel from 20 nations, is designed to respond rapidly to military crises and operations. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov denied Russian involvement following Tyner's arrest, according to the AP. "This arrest does not concern us in any way," Peskov said Nov. 11. "We don’t know what it’s connected to. We have nothing to do with this." According to a Nov. 13 statement from the U.S. Army, Tyner entered active-duty service in January 2008 and deployed to Afghanistan from December 2013 to December 2014, Qatar from July 2016 to July 2017, and Iraq from December 2019 to July 2020.

articles.title: Top IRGC commander in Iraq for talks amid Kataib Hezbollah tensions
articles.summary: Head of Iran’s IRGC Quds Force to attend meetings over alleged oil smuggling linked to pro-Iranian armed groups.
articles.body:
The commander of the Quds Force of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), Esmail Qaani, has arrived in Iraq to push for a solution amid simmering tensions near the town of Jurf al-Nasr, a stronghold of the pro-Iranian armed group Kataib Hezbollah, an Iraqi official has told Al Jazeera.

The Iraqi official explained that Qaani met with Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and held meetings with forces within the Coordination Framework—an umbrella for Shia Iraqi parties in the Iraqi parliament—in an effort to reach an agreement amid rising tensions over an investigation into suspected oil smuggling.

A leaked intelligence report last week had said two strategic oil pipelines running through the town of Jurf al-Nasr, located near Baghdad in the centre of the country, had effectively been tapped into.

Iraq recently launched a sweeping anti-corruption crackdown centred on the town, which allegedly harbours illicit oil refineries.

While officially framed as an initiative to protect public funds from a widespread smuggling network, some analysts say they believe the move is a highly calculated strategy to sever the financial arteries of pro-Iranian armed groups that refuse to integrate into the state apparatus.

The Iraqi source told Al Jazeera that the judicial committee has not yet reached an agreement with the factions to enter the area.

At least three leaders of the Coordination Framework also expressed their rejection of any armed clash or entry of federal forces before reaching a political understanding with Kataib Hezbollah, according to Al Jazeera’s correspondent in Iraq.

On Monday, al-Zaidi told military and security commanders to deploy additional forces around the town and to prepare for government troops to enter. The order would potentially bring the government and its troops into direct confrontation with the armed group.

Security agencies have also been instructed to prevent tankers carrying oil or petroleum products from leaving the area.

A senior Iraqi official previously told Al Jazeera that Kataib Hezbollah has until Friday to leave Jurf al-Nasr.

A Kataib Hezbollah commander told AFP, “I can state decisively and with absolute certainty that the dream they dream of the Kataib withdrawing [from Jurf al-Nasr] will not come true, not even over our dead bodies.”

Kataib Hezbollah, one of dozens of armed groups that have semi-official status in Iraq, denied the allegations on Sunday, saying that an inspection found no interference with pipelines.

The group has recently issued several statements criticising Iraq’s prime minister, accusing him of corruption and threatening his government.

It accused the government of “fabricating lies” about oil smuggling and of waging “the largest blackmail operation aimed at forcing” it to abandon its weapons.

Since coming into office, al-Zaidi has pledged to ensure that armed groups will hand over their weapons to the state.

articles.title: Cutting EV target risks UK missing climate targets, warns adviser
articles.summary: The UK could miss legally binding climate targets if EV targets are cut, an adviser warns
articles.body:
The UK is likely to miss legally binding climate targets if the government reduces electric vehicle (EV) targets, independent adviser the Climate Change Committee (CCC) has warned.

In a letter to Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander, the CCC argues that weakening the targets would result in "economic and energy security costs" and leave households "more exposed to volatile fossil fuel prices".

The CCC says that switching to an electric vehicle can save a typical household around £800 a year, with fewer people benefiting if the targets were watered down.

The warning comes after weeks of speculation that the government plans to announce changes to the EV targets. Government sources insist no decision has been made.

Under the current rules, a "zero emission vehicle" (ZEV) mandate requires 80% of new cars sold in the UK to be zero emission by 2030 and all new cars to meet that standard by 2035. Companies that fail to meet their ZEV mandate face a potential fine of £12,000 per car, although there are exemptions.

Industry groups have long complained the current rules impose too heavy a burden, calling instead for a "sustainable transition".

Latest data from trade body the Society of Motor Manufacturing and Traders (SMMT) shows that EVs, as well as plug-in hybrids, are driving growth in new car sales.

In the year so far, 26.6% of all new car registrations have been fully electric, the SMMT says, which is below the headline target of 33% for 2026.

But the industry as a whole appears on course to comply with this year's mandate once flexibilities are accounted for, according to analysis by New AutoMotive, a transport research organisation which supports the transition to electric cars

SMMT Chief Executive Mike Hawes accused the CCC of ignoring the costs of the targets it was defending.

"The industry cannot subsidise the transition indefinitely, which is why it is unified in seeking change," he said.

The CCC analysis also argued that weakening the targets would lead to a hole in the government's carbon savings that need to be made in order to meet its legally binding climate targets.

The CCC said the ZEV mandate "underpins the largest share of emissions reduction to 2037" in the government's net-zero plan. The climate targets set for 2033-2037 will be missed "without alternative action at the same scale", the CCC argued.

CCC analysis shows surface transport - which includes cars, vans and trucks - remains the country's highest carbon-emitting sector and one of the slowest to decarbonise.

Lord Deben, former CCC chairman, said going against CCC advice would "not be sensible" as it would "cost people money".

He said climate targets were "not random targets" and "if you don't reach them then you put yourselves in really serious danger of having climate change, which we can't handle".

articles.title: Ecuadorian fishermen sue Trump administration over drone strike
articles.summary: Crew say their boat was attacked by drones launched from US-operated vessel as part of ‘manifestly unlawful’ campaign.
articles.body:
A group of fishermen from Ecuador have sued the administration of United States President Donald Trump over a drone strike that sank their vessel and injured members of their crew in March.

The lawsuit, filed on Monday in a Pennsylvania federal court, seeks financial restitution and any additional relief the court considers just.

It also petitions the court to issue an order ending the Trump administration’s campaign of strikes targeting alleged drug trafficking boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific.

The complaint centres on the March 17 sinking of the fishing boat La Negra Francisca Duarte II, based in Ecuador.

“We filed the lawsuit because the boat was all we had. Nobody in Ecuador is helping us,” the ship’s captain, Hernan Flores, told the Reuters news agency. “They did all that damage to us, and by the grace of God, we’re alive.”

The government has not claimed responsibility for the strikes on La Negra Francisca Duarte II and two other Ecuadorian vessels that were attacked and sunk in recent months.

A report from the Washington Post in August, however, suggested that the vessels were targeted by the CIA as part of a secret overseas mission.

Other reports have raised the possibility of the attacks being conducted by a US government contractor or a regional ally.

The attacks appear to be similar to an ongoing campaign the US military has claimed credit for.

Since September 2025, the US government has publicly undertaken a series of boat strikes, with the aim of killing alleged “narcoterrorists”.

At least 244 people have been killed as part of that campaign, which experts have described as extrajudicial killing , in violation of international law.

The lawsuit filed on Monday alleges that two drones were launched from a vessel operated by the US in March and proceeded to attack La Negra Francisca Duarte II.

The boat was set ablaze, resulting in “serious burns” for two of the 16 crew members.

“All of the Plaintiffs ended up jumping off the ship and into the sea. They then found their way onto small emergency boats,” the filing said, calling the strike part of an “unprecedented and manifestly unlawful US military campaign”.

After the strike, the crew members say they made their way towards what they believed was a tuna fishing boat nearby but were met by armed men speaking English dressed in military uniforms.

Since Trump returned to the White House in 2025, he has launched a hardline campaign to combat drug trafficking into the US.

That push has coincided with a policy of expanding US military operations across Latin America, often in collaboration with right-wing political allies in the region.

But critics have raised concerns over transparency and potential rights abuses during such operations.

No suspects have been identified in the boat strike campaign undertaken by the US military, for instance, nor has any evidence been presented to the public.

Families, however, have stepped forward to claim the dead as their loved ones. Many have argued that the people killed in the boat strike campaign were not drug traffickers but fishermen and informal workers.

In December 2025, the family of the missing Colombian fisherman Alejandro Carranza filed a complaint about the boat strikes through the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, claiming his right to life had been violated.

A few weeks later, in January, the families of two workers from Trinidad and Tobago – Chad Joseph and Rishi Samaroo – filed a wrongful death lawsuit in a US federal court in Massachusetts. The men had reportedly been travelling home from Venezuela after taking work abroad.

But experts say that efforts to hold the US government to account will be difficult, given the lack of transparency surrounding the boat strikes.

The lethal boat strike campaign has continued in recent weeks, with a recent attack taking place on October 27.

The US government has also been involved in non-lethal interception efforts, stopping suspected drug-trafficking boats.

The watchdog group Human Rights Watch said that the US and Ecuador intercepted at least eight vessels between late August and mid-September, on the basis that they were being used to supply drug trafficking groups.

Of the 160 crew members on board those vessels, Human Rights Watch says that 56 were released without charge by court order, 40 were acquitted for lack of evidence, 50 are awaiting trial, and 14 were not formally charged.
